metais help templates — Writing templates: the environment, every filter, and
escaping.

A template is Liquid, in the dialect spec chapter 7 pins. The examples on this
page read these inputs:

  inputs.rows   [{"name": "b", "n": 2, "tag": "new"}, {"name": "a", "n": 1,
                "tag": null}]
  inputs.note   "line 1\nline 2"
  inputs.title  null: declared by the schema, and not supplied

  A loop over an input, with forloop:

    {% for row in inputs.rows -%}
    {{ forloop.index }} of {{ forloop.length }}: {{ row.name }}
    {% endfor -%}
  gives
    1 of 2: b
    2 of 2: a

  assign, a filter chain, and a test for nil:

    {% assign names = inputs.rows | map: "name" | sort -%}
    {% if inputs.title %}{{ inputs.title }}{% else %}Untitled{% endif %}
    {{ names | join: ", " }}
  gives
    Untitled
    a, b

  A partial, rendered once per element:

  templates/row.md holds
    - {{ row.name }} ({{ row.n }})
  and the template
    {% render "row.md" for inputs.rows as row %}
  gives
    - b (2)
    - a (1)

The environment:
  inputs   One member per declared input: its validated value, defaults applied.
           An optional input not supplied is nil.
  package  The manifest's metais, name, version, title, description, guide,
           authors, license and homepage, and digest, the package digest.
  output   In a template body: path, the output's path, and root, the relative
           prefix from its directory to the root of its tree ("", "../", ...).
  now      The render time the caller supplied, in UTC (2026-10-18T09:30:00Z),
           or nil. It is a template's only clock.
  sources  Where each input came from: origin is file, command-line or default;
           for a collection, each item's file name, stem and form.
  item     In an output with for_each only: the element being rendered.
  fan_out  Beside item: index, index0, rindex, rindex0, first, last, length,
           previous and next.

Names are strict. A name nothing binds is an error
(template.undefined_variable), and so is a property the schema does not declare
and the data does not hold (template.undefined_property), never an empty string.
A property the schema declares and the data omits is nil, and nil writes
nothing. Reading a property of nil is an error (template.nil_property), whatever
filter follows, default included; {% if a and a.b %} reads safely. Only nil and
false are false: 0, "", [] and {} are true, so {% if inputs.x %} asks whether x
was supplied. x == empty holds for an empty string, array or object; x == blank
also for nil, false and whitespace.

for loops over an array, a range (1..3) or an object, whose members it visits in
name order as [name, value] pairs; it takes limit:, offset: and reversed, and
else for an empty collection, and break and continue. Inside it, forloop has
index and index0 (from 1 and 0), rindex and rindex0 (from the end), first, last,
length, parentloop and name. {%- and -%} remove the whitespace before and after
a tag; nothing else is trimmed, so a tag alone on its line leaves its line feed.

assign binds a value and capture binds the text its block writes, for the rest
of the template; neither may take a global's name, forloop or tablerowloop
(template.reserved_name).

render "<path>" renders a partial: a template under templates/, named by its
full path there as a string literal ("parts/row.md"). It takes k: v parameters,
with x [as n], or for xs [as n], which renders it once per element and binds
forloop. A partial sees its parameters, its own bindings and the globals, and
none of its caller's assign, capture or loop variables. include is refused.

METAIS adds three tags, whose text is never escaped:
  embed       {% embed "<input>" %} writes an input's bytes exactly as its
              data-directory file holds them; index: n names an item of a
              collection.
  asset       {% asset "<path>" %} writes the relative path from the file being
              rendered to where the render copies an asset under assets/; as:
              "contents" writes its text, as: "base64" its bytes.
  provenance  {% provenance all %} writes one comment line naming the package,
              its version and digest, the inputs' digests, the tool and the
              render time when one was given; name parts to write fewer.

Filters:
Every filter of the dialect, with an example and what it gives. A filter's
keyword argument follows its positional ones: csv: "name", delimiter: ";". In
what an example gives, \n is a line feed.

Strings:
  append          Adds text at the end. {{ "doc" | append: ".md" }} gives doc.md
  prepend         Adds text at the start. {{ "md" | prepend: "." }} gives .md
  capitalize      Upper-cases the first character and lower-cases the rest.
                  {{ "hELLO" | capitalize }} gives Hello
  downcase        Lower-cases every letter, by Unicode's simple case mapping.
                  {{ "AbC" | downcase }} gives abc
  upcase          Upper-cases every letter, by Unicode's simple case mapping.
                  {{ "abc" | upcase }} gives ABC
  strip           Removes the whitespace at both ends.
                  {{ " a b " | strip }} gives a b
  lstrip          Removes the whitespace at the start.
                  {{ " a " | lstrip | append: "]" }} gives a ]
  rstrip          Removes the whitespace at the end.
                  {{ " a " | rstrip | prepend: "[" }} gives [ a
  squish          Strips both ends and makes each run of whitespace one space.
                  {{ inputs.note | squish }} gives line 1 line 2
  strip_html      Removes HTML tags.
                  {{ "<b>bold</b> text" | strip_html }} gives bold text
  strip_newlines  Removes every line break.
                  {{ inputs.note | strip_newlines }} gives line 1line 2
  newline_to_br   Writes <br /> before each line break.
                  {{ inputs.note | newline_to_br }} gives line 1<br />\nline 2
  remove          Removes every occurrence of a text.
                  {{ "a-b-c" | remove: "-" }} gives abc
  remove_first    Removes the first occurrence.
                  {{ "a-b-c" | remove_first: "-" }} gives ab-c
  remove_last     Removes the last occurrence.
                  {{ "a-b-c" | remove_last: "-" }} gives a-bc
  replace         Replaces every occurrence of a text with another.
                  {{ "a-b-c" | replace: "-", "+" }} gives a+b+c
  replace_first   Replaces the first occurrence.
                  {{ "a-b-c" | replace_first: "-", "+" }} gives a+b-c
  replace_last    Replaces the last occurrence.
                  {{ "a-b-c" | replace_last: "-", "+" }} gives a-b+c
  split           Splits a string into an array at each separator.
                  {{ "a,b,c" | split: "," | join: " " }} gives a b c
  truncate        Cuts a string to a number of characters, the ellipsis (...
                  unless given) included.
                  {{ "abcdefgh" | truncate: 6 }} gives abc...
  truncatewords   Keeps a number of words, then the ellipsis (... unless given).
                  {{ "one two three" | truncatewords: 2 }} gives one two...

Numbers (integers give an integer):
  abs             The absolute value. {{ -3 | abs }} gives 3
  ceil            Rounds up to an integer. {{ 1.2 | ceil }} gives 2
  floor           Rounds down to an integer. {{ 1.8 | floor }} gives 1
  round           Rounds half away from zero, to a number of decimal places when
                  given. {{ 2.5 | round }} gives 3
  plus            Adds; a float adds as the decimal it is written as.
                  {{ 0.1 | plus: 0.2 }} gives 0.3
  minus           Subtracts. {{ 5 | minus: 7 }} gives -2
  times           Multiplies. {{ 3 | times: 1.5 }} gives 4.5
  divided_by      Divides; two integers give the quotient rounded down.
                  {{ 7 | divided_by: 2 }} gives 3
  modulo          The remainder of the division rounded down.
                  {{ -7 | modulo: 2 }} gives 1
  at_least        The larger of the value and the argument.
                  {{ 3 | at_least: 5 }} gives 5
  at_most         The smaller of the value and the argument.
                  {{ 3 | at_most: 2 }} gives 2

Arrays:
  size            The length of a string, array or object; 0 for a number, a
                  boolean and nil. {{ "abc" | size }} gives 3
  first           The first element. {{ "a,b,c" | split: "," | first }} gives a
  last            The last element. {{ "a,b,c" | split: "," | last }} gives c
  join            The elements' texts, with a separator between them (a space
                  unless given).
                  {{ "a,b" | split: "," | join: " + " }} gives a + b
  reverse         The elements in reverse order.
                  {{ "a,b,c" | split: "," | reverse | join: "," }} gives c,b,a
  concat          The elements of both arrays.
                  {{ (1..2) | concat: (3..4) | join: "," }} gives 1,2,3,4
  compact         Drops nil elements, or the elements whose property is nil.
                  {{ inputs.rows | map: "tag" | compact | join: "," }} gives new
  uniq            Drops repeated elements.
                  {{ "a,b,a" | split: "," | uniq | join: "," }} gives a,b
  map             Each element's property.
                  {{ inputs.rows | map: "name" | join: "," }} gives b,a
  sort            Sorts, by a property when given.
                  {{ inputs.rows | sort: "n" | map: "name" | join: "," }}
                  gives a,b
  sort_natural    Sorts ignoring case.
                  {{ "b,C,a" | split: "," | sort_natural | join: "," }}
                  gives a,b,C
  slice           The element or character at an offset, or as many as a length
                  gives. {{ "abcdef" | slice: 1, 3 }} gives bcd
  sum             Adds the elements, or their property.
                  {{ inputs.rows | sum: "n" }} gives 3
  where           Keeps the elements whose property is truthy, or equals a
                  value.
                  {{ inputs.rows | where: "n", 1 | map: "name" | join }} gives a
  reject          Drops the elements whose property is truthy, or equals a
                  value.
                  {{ inputs.rows | reject: "tag" | map: "name" | join }} gives a
  has             Whether an element's property is truthy, or equals a value.
                  {{ inputs.rows | has: "name", "a" }} gives true
  find            The first element whose property is truthy, or equals a value.
                  {{ inputs.rows | find: "n", 1 | json }}
                  gives {"n":1,"name":"a","tag":null}
  find_index      The position of that element, from 0.
                  {{ inputs.rows | find_index: "name", "a" }} gives 1
  default         The value, or its argument when the value is nil, false, or an
                  empty string, array or object; allow_false: true keeps false.
                  {{ inputs.title | default: "Untitled" }} gives Untitled

Encoding (escape, h and escape_once give a safe value):
  escape          Writes & < > " and ' as HTML character references.
                  {{ "a < b" | escape }} gives a &lt; b
  h               escape, by another name. {{ "a & b" | h }} gives a &amp; b
  escape_once     escape, but leaves an & that already begins a character
                  reference.
                  {{ "&lt; & <" | escape_once }} gives &lt; &amp; &lt;
  url_encode      Percent-encodes a URL component; a space is +.
                  {{ "a b&c" | url_encode }} gives a+b%26c
  url_decode      Decodes what url_encode writes.
                  {{ "a+b%26c" | url_decode }} gives a b&c
  base64_encode   Base64. {{ "hi?" | base64_encode }} gives aGk/
  base64_decode   Decodes base64. {{ "aGk/" | base64_decode }} gives hi?
  base64_url_safe_encode
                  Base64 with - and _ for + and /.
                  {{ "hi?" | base64_url_safe_encode }} gives aGk_
  base64_url_safe_decode
                  Decodes URL-safe base64.
                  {{ "aGk_" | base64_url_safe_decode }} gives hi?

METAIS's own (spec chapter 8):
  json            RFC 8785 JSON: members in name order, no whitespace; indent: n
                  (1 to 8) pretty-prints.
                  {{ inputs.rows | last | json }}
                  gives {"n":1,"name":"a","tag":null}
  yaml            A YAML block document, members in name order, with no final
                  line feed; a string YAML could read otherwise, such as n, is
                  quoted.
                  {{ inputs.rows | first | yaml }}
                  gives "n": 2\nname: b\ntag: new
  csv             An array of objects as CSV, of the columns named or else every
                  member; header: false, headers: and delimiter: change it.
                  {{ inputs.rows | csv: "name", "n" }} gives name,n\nb,2\na,1\n
  markdown_table  An array of objects as a Markdown table, with the columns and
                  headers: of csv.
                  {{ inputs.rows | markdown_table: "name", "n" }}
                  gives | name | n |\n| --- | --- |\n| b | 2 |\n| a | 1 |\n
  json_script     json for a <script> element: < > & U+2028 and U+2029 written
                  as \u escapes; safe.
                  {{ "a&b" | json_script }} gives "a\u0026b"
  safe            Marks a value safe from escaping; only as the last filter of
                  {{ }} or echo. {{ "<b>" | safe }} gives <b>
  slug            Lower-case ASCII letters and digits joined by -; accents are
                  dropped, and a string with no slug is an error.
                  {{ "Hello, World!" | slug }} gives hello-world
  date            Formats an RFC 3339 date or date-time, or Unix seconds, in its
                  own offset, with a strftime format; spec chapter 8 lists the
                  directives.
                  {{ "2026-10-18T09:30:00+02:00" | date: "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %z" }}
                  gives 2026-10-18 09:30 +0200

Escaping:
An output's escape is none, the default, or html, set in metais.yaml beside its
template (escape: html); nothing is escaped unless it is set. In an html output,
the text of every value {{ }}, echo or cycle writes has & < > " and ' written as
character references; the template's own text, and what raw, embed, asset and
provenance write, are never escaped. A value is safe, and written as it is, when
its last filter is safe, escape, escape_once or json_script, or it is a capture
made in an html output. Safety does not pass through a later filter. A partial
is escaped as the output it renders into is.

Escaping does not make text safe inside a <script> element or a URL: data in a
<script> element goes through json_script, whose text can neither close the
element nor open an HTML comment, and a URL component through url_encode; the
dialect offers nothing else for those contexts. In an html output:

    <p>{{ "Fish & <Chips>" }}</p>
  gives
    <p>Fish &amp; &lt;Chips&gt;</p>

    {{ "<b>bold</b>" | safe }} {{ "<b>" | escape }}
  gives
    <b>bold</b> &lt;b&gt;

    {{ inputs.note | escape | newline_to_br | safe }}
  gives
    line 1<br />
    line 2

    <a href="/find?q={{ "a b&c" | url_encode }}">
  gives
    <a href="/find?q=a+b%26c">

    <script type="application/json">{{ "a</script>" | json_script }}</script>
  gives
    <script type="application/json">"a\u003c/script\u003e"</script>

'metais help manifest' gives the fields of metais.yaml; spec chapters 7, 8 and 9
give the environment, the filters and tags, and the outputs in full.
